sentences.en: For those of us who speak only one language, or maybe even speak two or three, the idea of learning 20 or 30 sounds impossible.
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些只会说一种语言，或者也许能说两种或三种语言的人来说，学20种或30种语言的想法听起来像是不可能的。

sentences.en: But there are people who have managed this remarkable feat.
sentences.zh: 但确实有人做成了这一非凡的壮举。

sentences.en: They're called hyperpolyglots.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为超级多语者。

sentences.en: There's no official definition of hyperpolyglotism.
sentences.zh: 目前对“超级多语者”并没有官方定义。

sentences.en: The International Association of Hyperpolyglots welcomes members who speak six or more languages, but some hyperpolyglots speak dozens with varying degrees of fluency.
sentences.zh: 国际超级多语者协会欢迎会说六种或更多语言的成员加入，但有些超级多语者能说几十种语言，流利程度各不相同。

sentences.en: So what sets hyperpolyglots apart?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟是什么让超级多语者与众不同呢？

sentences.en: Are they simply smarter than the rest of us, or harder working, or more motivated to learn?
sentences.zh: 他们是不是仅仅比我们其他人更聪明、更努力，或者学习动机更强？

sentences.en: If you put them in a functional magnetic resonance imaging scanner, do their brains look different from those of monolinguals or bilinguals?
sentences.zh: 如果把他们放进功能性磁共振成像扫描仪里，他们的大脑看起来会和单语者或双语者有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: And what might scientists discover about how the brain processes language by studying people with remarkable language abilities?
sentences.zh: 通过研究具有非凡语言能力的人，科学家们又能发现关于大脑如何处理语言的什么秘密呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《谈论心理学》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Ev Fedorenko.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是埃夫·费多连科博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Fedorenko is an associate professor in the Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology,
sentences.zh: 费多连科博士是麻省理工学院大脑与认知科学系的副教授，

sentences.en: where she explores how people understand and produce language.
sentences.zh: 她在那里探索人们如何理解和产生语言。

sentences.en: She uses brain imaging and other research methods to study healthy individuals and people with language-related brain disorders, as well as hyperpolyglots.
sentences.zh: 她利用脑成像和其他研究方法来研究健康个体、有语言相关脑部疾病的患者，以及超级多语者。

sentences.en: Among the questions she's interested in are, what's the relationship between language and other cognitive abilities?
sentences.zh: 她感兴趣的问题包括：语言与其他认知能力之间有什么关系？

sentences.en: Can we think without language?
sentences.zh: 我们能否在没有语言的情况下进行思考？

sentences.en: What is the organization of the language system in our brain, and how does it emerge in childhood and change over the course of a lifetime?
sentences.zh: 我们大脑中的语言系统是如何组织的？它在童年时期是如何萌芽并在整个一生中发生变化的？

sentences.en: We'll try to touch on those topics today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天会尽量涉及这些话题。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Fedorenko.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你加入我们，费多连科博士。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很荣幸能来到这里。

sentences.en: So, as I indicated, your research is much broader than hyperpolyglotism, but let's start with that topic because it's so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 那么，正如我所指出的，你的研究范围远不止超级多语者，但让我们先从这个话题开始，因为它太迷人了。

sentences.en: How did you become interested in studying people who speak dozens of languages, and why does studying this extremely rare ability,
sentences.zh: 你是怎么对研究那些说几十种语言的人产生兴趣的？为什么研究这种极端罕见的能力——

sentences.en: why is this a useful way to learn more about language and the brain?
sentences.zh: 为什么这是深入了解语言和大腦的一种有效途径？

sentences.en: As you know, for many years, centuries, really, researchers have studied individuals with language probleMs.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，多年来，实际上几个世纪以来，研究人员一直在研究有语言问题的人。

sentences.en: And the intuition there is very clear.
sentences.zh: 这里的直觉非常明确。

sentences.en: We can learn a lot about how something works by looking at ways in which it can break or malfunction.
sentences.zh: 通过观察事物如何损坏或发生故障，我们可以深入了解它的运作原理。

sentences.en: And we have learned a lot from individuals with both developmental disorders like autism,
sentences.zh: 我们已经从自闭症等发育障碍患者身上学到了很多，

sentences.en: as well as acquired disorders like aphasia due to stroke or degeneration or head trauma or something like that.
sentences.zh: 也从诸如中风、大脑退化或头部创伤等原因导致的失语症等获得性障碍患者身上学到了很多。

sentences.en: But there is this other extreme in any cognitive ability or perceptual ability you can think of.
sentences.zh: 但你能想到的任何认知能力或感知能力，都存在另一个极端。

sentences.en: There is this extreme where it seems that some tail of the population, some small number of individuals in the population, are especially good at something.
sentences.zh: 在这个极端里，似乎人口中的某个尾端群体、极少数的个人特别擅长某事。

sentences.en: And it's kind of interesting to think about what it means to be good at language.
sentences.zh: 思考“擅长语言”意味着什么，是一件挺有意思的事。

sentences.en: And there's probably many different ways in which you can be good at language.
sentences.zh: 擅长语言的方式可能有很多种。

sentences.en: But it certainly seems that this ability to acquire multiple languages, multiple mappings between meanings and forms,
sentences.zh: 但显然，这种习得多种语言、在意义和形式（比如词汇和结构）之间建立多种对应关系的能力，

sentences.en: like words and constructions, is certainly one way in which you can be good at language.
sentences.zh: 绝对是擅长语言的一种方式。

sentences.en: And some people seem to have a propensity for this, or at least in one way or another become hyperpolyglots.
sentences.zh: 有些人似乎对这方面很有天赋，或者至少以某种方式成为了超级多语者。

sentences.en: And so we get interested and maybe we can learn something about how the typical system works, but also studying this other extreme of linguistic abilities.
sentences.zh: 因此我们产生了兴趣，也许我们不仅能通过研究这种语言能力的另一个极端来了解典型系统的运作方式，还能学到更多。

sentences.en: Do we have any idea how rare hyperpolyglotism is?
sentences.zh: 我们对超级多语者的稀少程度有什么概念吗？

sentences.en: And are there particular characteristics of hyperpolyglots, such as are they mostly men?
sentences.zh: 超级多语者有没有什么独特的特征？比如他们大多是男性吗？

sentences.en: Do they tend to be ambidextrous?
sentences.zh: 他们往往是双撇子吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what's unique about them in addition to their language ability?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，除了语言能力之外，他们还有什么独特之处？

sentences.en: The prevalence is very hard to estimate.
sentences.zh: 这种现象的患病率很难估计。

sentences.en: There are now a few of these organizations that try to kind of bring together polyglots.
sentences.zh: 现在有一些这样的组织，试图将多语者聚集在一起。

sentences.en: But I still think there's many people who kind of do this on their own.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然认为，有很多人是独自默默进行这件事的。

sentences.en: And Von Smith, who recently was covered in the Washington Post article, is one of those people, right?
sentences.zh: 最近《华盛顿邮报》文章中报道的冯·史密斯就是其中之一，对吧？

sentences.en: That he just does it and nobody knows.
sentences.zh: 他只是自己学，谁也不知道。

sentences.en: He doesn't belong to any societies or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 他不加入任何社团或类似的东西。

sentences.en: So I think it's probably whatever estimates exist out there are probably underestimates.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为现有的任何估计可能都偏低。

sentences.en: In terms of characteristics, it's a surprisingly heterogeneous population.
sentences.zh: 就特征而言，这是一个出人意料的异质群体。

sentences.en: One thing that seems to hold for many people is that, and this was counterintuitive to me, is that they're not typically individuals who grew up in multilingual societies.
sentences.zh: 有一点似乎适用于许多人，而且这对我来说有点反直觉，那就是他们通常并不是在多语社会中长大的孩子。

sentences.en: So there are some countries like, you know, the Netherlands, where most kids grow up speaking three languages, or Switzerland, or, you know, parts of India.
sentences.zh: 所以有些国家，你知道的，比如荷兰，大多数孩子长大后会说三种语言，或者是瑞士，或者印度的一些地区。

sentences.en: They typically grow up in relatively monolingual societies or societies where there's one dominant language, like Russia has a high proportion of polyglots.
sentences.zh: 他们通常在相对单一语言的社会中长大，或者在一个只有一种主导语言的社会中长大，比如俄罗斯的比例很高。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: does as well.
sentences.zh: 也是如此。

sentences.en: So they grow up monolingual.
sentences.zh: 所以他们长大时是单语的。

sentences.en: And then at some point, they just get interested in learning languages and maybe start with like
sentences.zh: 然后在某个时候，他们开始对学习语言产生兴趣，也许是从

sentences.en: a typical class in school and then realize that they like doing this or are good at it.
sentences.zh: 学校里的一门普通课程开始，然后发现自己喜欢做这件事或者很擅长。

sentences.en: And then just kind of keep going with this.
sentences.zh: 接着就顺着这条路继续学下去了。

sentences.en: But otherwise, it's a very heterogeneous group of people.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，这是一群非常多元化的人。

sentences.en: Some are really extroverted and can learn through kind of social interaction with native speakers.
sentences.zh: 有些性格非常外向，可以通过与母语者的社交互动来学习。

sentences.en: Some are quite introverted and learn primarily from books.
sentences.zh: 有些相当内向，主要通过书本学习。

sentences.en: It seems that the ways in which they're good at learning languages is also different.
sentences.zh: 他们擅长学习语言的方式似乎也各不相同。

sentences.en: We can talk more about that.
sentences.zh: 我们可以多聊聊这个。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think more of the people that we've tested so far are males, but I would not attribute
sentences.zh: 不过是的，我认为我们迄今为止测试过的人中男性更多一些，但我不会把

sentences.en: much to that just because historically in our society, males have had more encouragement for certain things.
sentences.zh: 这归因于太多原因，只是因为在历史上我们的社会中，男性在某些事情上得到了更多的鼓励。

sentences.en: And I think there's still biases these days so that girls may be not as much encouraged or something like this.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为如今仍然存在偏见，导致女孩可能没有得到那么多的鼓励或类似的支持。

sentences.en: And so I wouldn't make, I would be very cautious in making any claims about gender biases until
sentences.zh: 因此我不会轻易下结论，在我们的社会在消除性别歧视方面变得足够健康、

sentences.en: our society is healthy enough in terms of the lack of sexism when we can assess these things more fairly.
sentences.zh: 让我们能够更公平地评估这些事情之前，我在对性别偏见做出任何断言时都会非常谨慎。

sentences.en: Ah, yes, we're waiting for that day.
sentences.zh: 啊，是的，我们正在等待那一天的到来。

sentences.en: So much of your research uses fMRI brain imaging.
sentences.zh: 你的很多研究都使用了fMRI脑成像技术。

sentences.en: What have you found when you look at the brains of hyperpolyglots?
sentences.zh: 当你观察超级多语者的大脑时，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: How do their brains look or function differently compared with the brains of people who only speak one or two languages?
sentences.zh: 与只会说一种或两种语言的人的大脑相比，他们的大脑在外观或功能上有何不同？

sentences.en: So, of course, for this comparison, if we're comparing polyglots and typical individuals, we have to look at the responses at these participants' native language, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，为了进行这种比较，如果我们要在多语者和普通人之间作对比，我们必须看这些参与者在其母语上的反应，对吧？

sentences.en: Because otherwise, it's difficult to make comparisons because there will be differences in proficiency.
sentences.zh: 否则很难进行比较，因为熟练程度会有所不同。

sentences.en: But I can take you, you're a native speaker of English, and I can take a polyglot whose native language is also English, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果我选你，你是英语母语者，然后我选一个母语也是英语的多语者，对吧？

sentences.en: And if you look at the neural responses to native language, we find that in hyperpolyglots,
sentences.zh: 如果你观察他们对母语的神经反应，我们会发现在超级多语者中，

sentences.en: the language system looks smaller than in typical individuals, meaning the amount of territory that
sentences.zh: 他们的语言系统看起来比普通人更小，这意味着在他们处理语言时，

sentences.en: kind of lights up, quote-unquote, in the brain when they process language is smaller, and the
sentences.zh: 在大脑中“亮起来”（加引号）的区域面积更小，并且

sentences.en: regions that respond to language respond less strongly when they process language compared to you or me.
sentences.zh: 当他们处理语言时，对语言有反应的区域其反应强度也比你或我更弱。

sentences.en: And this was originally an accidental discovery.
sentences.zh: 这最初是一个意外的发现。

sentences.en: We had somebody contact us a bunch of years ago now and said, I have a son who is a polyglot.
sentences.zh: 好几年前有人联系我们，说：“我有个儿子是个多语者。”

sentences.en: He's learning, you know, he had like 20 or something languages.
sentences.zh: 他正在学……他当时会大概20种左右的语言。

sentences.en: Would you be interested in testing him?
sentences.zh: 你们有兴趣测试他吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, I was young.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我当时很年轻。

sentences.en: I guess I'm still pretty young, but I was younger and very interested broadly in how language works in the brain.
sentences.zh: 我想我现在也挺年轻的，但那时更年轻，并且对语言在人脑中如何运作有着广泛的浓厚兴趣。

sentences.en: And so I said, yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 所以我说：“行啊，没问题。”

sentences.en: We had some extra resources at the time.
sentences.zh: 我们当时有一些额外的资源。

sentences.en: And so we brought him out and we scanned him on our usual paradigMs.
sentences.zh: 于是我们把他请来，用我们常规的实验范式对他进行了扫描。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, his language, which is look really wimpy.
sentences.zh: 结果出人意料，他的语言区看起来非常弱小。

sentences.en: And I was like, hmm, that's strange.
sentences.zh: 当时我想：“嗯，这太奇怪了。”

sentences.en: You might expect a priority, right?
sentences.zh: 按先验推断，你可能会预料到，对吧？

sentences.en: That somebody who is really good at language will have like these robust, strongly responding areas.
sentences.zh: 一个真正擅长语言的人应该拥有那种健硕、反应强烈的区域。

sentences.en: And the responses look small.
sentences.zh: 但这些反应看起来却很小。

sentences.en: And we tested them again the next stage to make sure things are replicable.
sentences.zh: 我们在第二天又测试了他们一次，以确保结果具有可重复性。

sentences.en: And again, they look small.
sentences.zh: 结果看起来还是那么小。

sentences.en: And I'm like, oh, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 然后我想：“哦，这真有趣。”

sentences.en: And then I started talking to other people working in different domains.
sentences.zh: 接着我开始和在不同领域工作的其他人交流。

sentences.en: And people brought up examples of motor learning.
sentences.zh: 人们提到了运动学习的例子。

sentences.en: And they said, well, actually, that's kind of what happens when you learn new motor skills.
sentences.zh: 他们说：“其实，当你学习新的运动技能时，发生的就是这种情况。”

sentences.en: So if I teach you some complicated motor skill, like some tracing of complex patterns or something,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我教你一些复杂的运动技能，比如描摹一些复杂的图案或者别的什么，

sentences.en: and I have you do it initially, you'll have big chunks of your motor cortex respond as you're still kind of getting better.
sentences.zh: 一开始让你去做，当你还在逐渐熟练的过程中时，你的运动皮层会有很大一部分做出反应。

sentences.en: And as you get more and more proficient and it becomes kind of more automated, the amount of motor cortex that you have to recruit becomes smaller.
sentences.zh: 而随着你越来越熟练，它变得越来越自动化时，你所需要调动的运动皮层数量就会变小。

sentences.en: So you don't need to use as much tissue to achieve the same level of performance.
sentences.zh: 所以你不需要使用那么多的脑组织就能达到相同的表现水平。

sentences.en: And so maybe something similar is happening here.
sentences.zh: 也许这里也发生了类似的事情。

sentences.en: So that's the parallel we drew in interpreting these results.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在解释这些结果时做出的类比。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: And I should say that, you know, then eventually we kind of got other polyglots contact us.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，最终有其他多语者联系了我们。

sentences.en: We found a few local ones at MIT and surrounding areas.
sentences.zh: 我们在麻省理工学院及周边地区找到了几个本地的多语者。

sentences.en: And then we ended up with like a set of 20.
sentences.zh: 最后我们凑齐了一组20人。

sentences.en: And that finding holds across them.
sentences.zh: 这个发现在他们身上都成立。

sentences.en: So the like looking at the distribution of the sizes of the language areas in that population
sentences.zh: 因此，观察该人群中语言区域大小的分布，

sentences.en: is definitely shifted to the smaller side compared to this large normative set that we have now, like hundreds of typical participants.
sentences.zh: 与我们现在拥有的包含数百名典型参与者的大型常模数据集相比，确实向较小的一侧偏移了。

sentences.en: So what else sets hyperpolyglots apart?
sentences.zh: 那么，还有什么让超级多语者与众不同？

sentences.en: Are they generally extremely smart in other ways?
sentences.zh: 他们在其他方面通常也极其聪明吗？

sentences.en: Or is their talent just restricted to language?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们的天赋仅限于语言？

sentences.en: Do they have to study hard to learn languages in the way that other adults do?
sentences.zh: 他们是否必须像其他成年人那样努力学习语言？

sentences.en: Or does it come more easily and naturally to them the way that it might to children?
sentences.zh: 还是说这就像对儿童那样，对他们来说更容易、更自然？

sentences.en: In the study that, in the one study we published on the neural responses to native language in polyglots in typical individuals, we actually matched for IQ.
sentences.zh: 在我们发表的关于多语者与普通人母语神经反应的那项研究中，我们实际上控制了智商变量。

sentences.en: So the difference that we observed holds in spite of similar levels of kind of general fluid intelligence.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管一般流体智力水平相似，我们观察到的差异依然存在。

sentences.en: We also looked at the responses, neural responses in the brain system that kind of supports general fluid reasoning.
sentences.zh: 我们还观察了支持一般流体推理的大脑系统中的神经反应。

sentences.en: And those regions looked similar in size.
sentences.zh: 这些区域在大小上看起来很相似。

sentences.en: So it's not like their whole brain is efficient, no matter what system you look at.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说无论你看哪个系统，他们整个大脑都很高效。

sentences.en: It seems specific to language.
sentences.zh: 这种现象似乎是针对语言特有的。

sentences.en: And in general, we and others have found that those two systems are quite separate.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我们和其他人发现这两个系统是相当独立的。

sentences.en: The system that supports thinking and reasoning and the system that supports language processing.
sentences.zh: 支持思考和推理的系统，以及支持语言处理的系统。

sentences.en: But in terms of what makes them different, I don't think we know quite yet.
sentences.zh: 但至于是什么让他们与众不同，我觉得我们目前还不是很清楚。

sentences.en: So it's undeniable that there are some people for whom learning languages is easier than others.
sentences.zh: 因此不可否认的是，对某些人来说，学语言确实比对其他人更容易。

sentences.en: That just that variability is there.
sentences.zh: 这种差异确实存在。

sentences.en: I myself learned a lot of languages until I moved to the US and it all got kind of dormant and forgotten.
sentences.zh: 我自己以前也学过很多语言，直到我搬到美国，它们就变得有些荒废和被遗忘了。

sentences.en: But growing up, I learned that and I love doing it and it was easy.
sentences.zh: 但在成长过程中，我学过那些语言，我喜欢这么做，而且觉得很容易。

sentences.en: Like I enjoyed doing it and it kind of came naturally.
sentences.zh: 就像我乐在其中，而且一切水到渠成。

sentences.en: I could remember things easily.
sentences.zh: 我能轻易记住东西。

sentences.en: I could decipher grammatical patterns.
sentences.zh: 我能破解语法规律。

sentences.en: So and you'll hear other people talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以你会听到其他人也这么说。

sentences.en: They're like, yeah, it seems like I get like a good feel for a language very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得：“对啊，我似乎能非常快地对一门语言产生一种好感。”

sentences.en: Like I can kind of understand which words are related, construct things.
sentences.zh: 比如我能大致理解哪些词是相关的，如何构建句子。

sentences.en: Once I learn a few words, construct things much more easily than my peers seem to.
sentences.zh: 一旦我学会几个词，构建起内容来就比身处同一环境中的同龄人似乎要容易得多。

sentences.en: They're learning me in the same environment or something like that.
sentences.zh: 他们在相同的环境中学习之类的。

sentences.en: But there's also, again, quite surprisingly, there's also hyperpolyglots who are pretty adamant that they don't have any special talent.
sentences.zh: 但同样出人意料的是，也有一些超级多语者非常坚决地表示他们没有任何特殊天赋。

sentences.en: Again, maybe introspection is not the best way to, but they just say, I just like doing it.
sentences.zh: 当然，内省也许并不是最好的方法，但他们只是说：“我就是喜欢这么做。”

sentences.en: It's like a hobby for me.
sentences.zh: “这就像是我的爱好。”

sentences.en: I spend a lot of time doing this and I get better, but I don't think I'm linguistically gifted in any way.
sentences.zh: “我花了很多时间做这件事，然后变得更好了，但我并不觉得自己有什么语言天赋。”

sentences.en: I just kind of spend a lot of time.
sentences.zh: “我只是花了很多时间。”

sentences.en: Like I spend, you know, 20 minutes each day or whatever, you know, an hour a week on each of my 20 or 30 languages.
sentences.zh: “比如我每天花20分钟，或者对我的20种、30种语言每种每周花一小时。”

sentences.en: And I get good because people get good with practice, right?
sentences.zh: “然后我就变好了，因为通过练习大家都会变好，对吧？”

sentences.en: Like every, anybody will get good.
sentences.zh: “就像任何人通过练习都会变好一样。”

sentences.en: Almost anybody will get good with practice on almost any task.
sentences.zh: 几乎任何人只要多加练习，在几乎任何任务上都能变得优秀。

sentences.en: But of course there is this underlying variability and it's possible that some of the kind
sentences.zh: 但当然，这种潜在的差异是客观存在的，而且可能存在某些

sentences.en: of more extreme hyperpolyglots who achieve proficiency in, you know, upward of 20 languages, maybe it's some combination of some innate talent, if you wish.
sentences.zh: 更极端的超级多语者，他们掌握了，你知道的，20种以上的语言，也许这可以看作是某种先天天赋的结合。

sentences.en: People sometimes get upset about the use of terms like that, but, you know, whatever, innate biases to be good at language, whatever.
sentences.zh: 人们有时会对这种术语的使用感到反感，但不管怎样，你知道的，就是那种擅长语言的先天倾向之类的。

sentences.en: And a lot of practice.
sentences.zh: 再加上大量的练习。

sentences.en: And then maybe combine those things together.
sentences.zh: 然后也许把这些因素结合在一起。

sentences.en: That you can kind of get to the real extreme of that ability to learn so many different mappings between meanings and forMs.
sentences.zh: 你就能达到那种学习能力的极端巅峰，能够应对意义与形式之间如此之多的不同对应关系。

sentences.en: But I think there's a lot we don't understand.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们还有很多不了解的地方。

sentences.en: This is a very understudied population.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极少被研究的人群。

sentences.en: It's sad.
sentences.zh: 这挺遗憾的。

sentences.en: There's not many of them and they're not like all in one area or something.
sentences.zh: 他们人数不多，而且也不是集中在某个地方之类的。

sentences.en: So it's a pretty challenging group to study.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个相当具有挑战性的研究群体。

sentences.en: But I'm hoping that some of the stuff we've been doing recently will inspire others to try to characterize them kind of more broadly and in all sorts of other ways.
sentences.zh: 但我希望我们最近做的一些工作能激励其他人，尝试以更广泛、更全面的方式来对他们进行特征描述。

sentences.en: Aside from just neural responses.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅局限于神经反应。

sentences.en: So I thought it was interesting in preparing to talk to you that there isn't a connection between, say, musical ability and language ability.
sentences.zh: 所以在准备与你对话时，我发现了一件有趣的事，那就是音乐能力和语言能力之间似乎并没有什么联系。

sentences.en: Because you would think there are some languages that are very tonal and they almost sound like music and yet there isn't a connection.
sentences.zh: 因为你会觉得有些语言声调感极强，听起来几乎就像音乐一样，然而它们之间却并没有联系。

sentences.en: Do you have any understanding of why that might be?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么理解吗？

sentences.en: It just seems counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 这似乎有违直觉。

sentences.en: To clarify, the lack of, so the dissociation between language and music is happening at the level of kind of language understanding.
sentences.zh: 澄清一下，这种缺乏联系的现象，也就是语言和音乐之间的分离，发生在语言理解的层面上。

sentences.en: So the system that you use to understand and produce language, so to kind of infer meanings
sentences.zh: 因此，你用来理解和产出语言的系统，也就是用来从词语序列中

sentences.en: from sequences of words and convert your thoughts into sequences of words, that system is totally separate from music.
sentences.zh: 推断含义，并将你的想法转化为词语序列的系统，与音乐是完全无关的。

sentences.en: And this is contra many proposals.
sentences.zh: 这与许多原有的提议相悖。

sentences.en: And that is now, I think, we and a few other groups have strong evidence that the language
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为我们和其他几个研究小组都有强有力的证据表明，

sentences.en: regions are just not working at all when you're listening to music, even if it's complex and
sentences.zh: 当你听音乐时，语言区域根本完全没有在工作，哪怕音乐很复杂、

sentences.en: structured and has all sorts of properties that people argue it may be shared between music and language.
sentences.zh: 很有结构，并且具备人们认为可能在音乐和语言之间共享的各种属性。

sentences.en: But there is some overlap at the lower level auditory processing.
sentences.zh: 但在较低水平的听觉处理上确实有一些重叠。

sentences.en: So there is, for example, a part of our auditory cortex that cares about pitched sounds.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们的听觉皮层中有一个部分专门关注有音高的声音。

sentences.en: So any kind of pitch sounds, it can be a train horn or a speech segment or a piece of music.
sentences.zh: 所以任何种类的音高声音，无论是火车汽笛、语音片段还是一段音乐。

sentences.en: And any time there is kind of pitch modulation, harmonics present, that region is active.
sentences.zh: 只要有音高调制或谐波出现，那个区域就会被激活。

sentences.en: And so through that shared machinery, there are indeed some transfer effects so that musicians, for example, have an easier time learning tonal languages.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过这种共享的机制，确实存在一些迁移效应，比如音乐家在学习声调语言时会更容易。

sentences.en: Those effects have been reported for quite a while.
sentences.zh: 这些效应已经被报道了相当长的一段时间。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem that being a musician, so having a lot of practice with music or being musically
sentences.zh: 但成为音乐家——也就是有大量音乐实践经验，或者有音乐天赋，

sentences.en: talented or having things like absolute pitch makes you better at learning languages in general.
sentences.zh: 或者拥有绝对音高之类特质——似乎并不会让你在总体上更擅长学习语言。

sentences.en: But it will help with the aspects of language that rely on that ability that you're training out, which is paying attention to pitch and the signal.
sentences.zh: 但它会帮助你掌握语言中依赖于你正在训练的那种能力的部分，也就是对声音中的音高和信号保持敏感。

sentences.en: But it doesn't seem like a general thing.
sentences.zh: 但这似乎并不是一种普遍的提升。

sentences.en: Why is it do scientists know why babies and children can learn language so easily and that it becomes more difficult as we get older?
sentences.zh: 科学家们是否知道为什么婴儿和儿童能如此轻易地学习语言，而随着年龄增长却变得越来越难？

sentences.en: I'm sure it's hard for you to get little babies and put them in fMRI machines, but I know you've looked at some kids.
sentences.zh: 我确信让你去找小婴儿并把他们放进fMRI机器里会很困难，但我知道你们确实观察过一些孩子。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a million dollar question that is still very much debated.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个价值百万美元的问题，目前仍在激烈争论中。

sentences.en: So a lot of things change when you're learning a language as a kid and you're learning a language as an adult.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你作为儿童学习语言与作为成年人学习语言时，有很多事情都发生了变化。

sentences.en: For one, when you come into the world, you don't know anything about the world, right?
sentences.zh: 首先，当你来到这个世界时，你对这个世界一无所知，对吧？

sentences.en: So at the same time, as you get it, starting to get exposure to speech, you're also learning all sorts of things about the world, the social agents in the world, the physical
sentences.zh: 所以与此同时，当你开始接触语音时，你也在了解关于这个世界的各种事物、世界上的社会主体、世界的物理

sentences.en: properties of the world, the objects, how they interact.
sentences.zh: 属性、各种物体以及它们是如何相互作用的。

sentences.en: And at the same time, you're hearing linguistic signals or watching them if you're a baby learning sign language.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你也在听取语言信号，或者如果你是一个学习手语的婴儿，你就在观察它们。

sentences.en: And then at some point, you're, you know, as a baby, you start noticing that there's some non-randomness so that like every time, you know, your daddy says ball, there seems to be
sentences.zh: 然后在某个时刻，作为一个婴儿，你开始注意到其中存在某种非随机性，比如每次你爸爸说“球”的时候，

sentences.en: this round thing around, right?
sentences.zh: 周围似乎总会有这么一个圆乎乎的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, you don't know the word for round, but you kind of know just that there's a thing like that looks like this round thing around.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你当时并不知道“圆”这个词，但你大概知道有这么一个长得像这种圆乎乎东西的存在。

sentences.en: And eventually, I think it must click for babies that there is this non-trivial correspondence between these things that we're
sentences.zh: 最终，我想婴儿们一定会突然开窍：我们用嘴巴发出的声音，或者如果我们是手语使用者，

sentences.en: making, the sounds that we're making with our mouths or with our hands, if we're a signer, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 用手做出的动作，这些东西与周围环境之间存在着这种非同寻常的对应关系。

sentences.en: And then once that clicks, then I think, you know, like language just kind of goes through the roof and word learning happens.
sentences.zh: 而一旦这一点开窍了，那么我认为，语言能力就会像火箭般飞升，词汇学习随之发生。

sentences.en: And eventually they start composing words and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 最终他们开始组合词汇，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Why we lose the ability to learn language as easily, like I said, very debated.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会失去轻松学习语言的能力，就像我说的，这存在很大争议。

sentences.en: So for one, you already have a set of mappings, right?
sentences.zh: 首先，你已经有了一套映射关系，对吧？

sentences.en: You've learned a language.
sentences.zh: 你已经学会了一门语言。

sentences.en: So there's already a fixed system there of how things map.
sentences.zh: 所以那里已经有了一个固定的系统来决定事物是如何映射的。

sentences.en: So learning a system on top of that, another set of mappings on top of that may be harder.
sentences.zh: 因此，在此基础之上再去学习另一个系统、另一套映射关系可能会更难。

sentences.en: I always make this point that I haven't heard others focus on as much, but the way that you learn a second language is typically very, very different.
sentences.zh: 我总是提出这一点，但我没怎么听到其他人这么关注，那就是你学习第二语言的方式通常非常非常不同。

sentences.en: So we actually don't have very well controlled experiments of similar environments for first and later acquired languages.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们并没有对第一语言和后来习得的语言进行过控制良好的相似环境实验。

sentences.en: Because, you know, if you've had kids, I have a four-year-old.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，如果你带过孩子，我有一个四岁的孩子。

sentences.en: So we just went through this whole language learning thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们刚刚经历了整个语言学习的过程。

sentences.en: If you're a baby, every time you're awake, there's a face in front of your face and it's making speech sounds at you, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个婴儿，你醒着的每一刻，你的面前都有一张脸，它在对你发出语音，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, and it, and, and it loves you.
sentences.zh: 而且它、它、它爱着你。

sentences.en: Like all these caregivers around you, they love you and they interact with you every time you're awake, like pretty much every time you're awake, there is some kind of language.
sentences.zh: 就像你周围的所有照顾者一样，他们爱你，在你醒着的每一刻都与你互动，几乎在你醒着的每一刻，都有某种语言存在。

sentences.en: It's a very different experience from taking a class.
sentences.zh: 这与去上课有着截然不同的体验。

sentences.en: And even in immersion, right?
sentences.zh: 即使是在沉浸式环境中也是如此，对吧？

sentences.en: Like you may go to Paris, you're sitting in a cafe, somebody will occasionally talk to you, but it's not like you're constantly
sentences.zh: 比如你去巴黎，坐在咖啡馆里，偶尔有人会跟你说话，但这并不意味着你一直在

sentences.en: having people who love you try to teach you the skill so that we can interact better, right?
sentences.zh: 有爱你的人试图教你这项技能，好让我们能更好地互动，对吧？

sentences.en: It's just a very different, it's a very bad, poorly controlled comparison.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一种完全不同的、非常糟糕且控制不佳的对比。

sentences.en: And there are some claims that, um, underdeveloped executive abilities early on may be helpful, um, that maybe, um, kind of interfere later on.
sentences.zh: 还有一些观点认为，早期执行功能的不成熟可能是有帮助的，也许在后期会产生某种干扰。

sentences.en: There is some claims that babies initially, um, don't have the propensity.
sentences.zh: 还有观点认为，婴儿最初不具备这种倾向。

sentences.en: So speech is a continuous, if we're talking about spoken language, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们讨论的是口语，语音本身是连续的，对吧？

sentences.en: There's no boundaries between words.
sentences.zh: 词与词之间没有界限。

sentences.en: And so kids will kind of hear continuous chunks of speech, sometimes in pretty large chunks.
sentences.zh: 因此，孩子们听到的往往是连续的语音块，有时甚至是非常大的语块。

sentences.en: They don't have the words within that chunk.
sentences.zh: 他们并不知道那个语块内部有哪些具体的词。

sentences.en: Um, and people like Inbal Arnon, um, in Israel has argued that, uh, actually not always parsing things into individual words may help you initially bootstrap the system,
sentences.zh: 以色列的英巴尔·阿农等人认为，事实上，并非总把语言解析成单个词，反而可能有助于你最初启动这个系统，

sentences.en: because you're learning bigger chunks from which you can potentially more easily infer, um, kind of multi-word relationships and things like that.
sentences.zh: 因为你正在学习更大的语块，从中你可以更容易地推断出多词之间的关系之类的事情。

sentences.en: Because once you're learning, once you're grown up, you understand words, right?
sentences.zh: 因为一旦你长大成人，你就理解了词汇，对吧？

sentences.en: You understand that there's words.
sentences.zh: 你明白世界上有“词”这回事。

sentences.en: And so when you're learning a second language, you learn everything in individual words, as opposed to paying attention to like phrases and
sentences.zh: 所以当你学习第二语言时，你是在学习每一个独立的词，而不是去关注那些短语和

sentences.en: constructions where you may benefit from the fact that a certain sequence of words always happens together.
sentences.zh: 结构，在那些结构中，你本可以受益于这样一个事实：某些词序总是连在一起出现。

sentences.en: So there's all sorts of hypotheses out there.
sentences.zh: 所以现在有各种各样的假设。

sentences.en: Um, in terms of the evidence, kind of the larger scale studies that do exist, do suggest that there is a drop in your ability to learn,
sentences.zh: 就证据而言，现有的较大规模研究确实表明，在青春期之后（大约15、16岁，也就是青春期后期），

sentences.en: um, languages in a native-like way after around puberty, like 15, 16, kind of late puberty.
sentences.zh: 你以母语般的方式学习语言的能力确实会出现下降。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: but again, there's only some abilities that are affected.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，只有某些能力会受到影响。

sentences.en: So grammar and, um, sensory motor stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如语法以及感觉运动方面。

sentences.en: So accents, accent is something that's really hard to lose, um, after that time period.
sentences.zh: 所以口音，口音在这个时期之后确实很难改变。

sentences.en: In terms of learning words, you can kind of keep learning words, uh, no matter how old you are.
sentences.zh: 至于学习词汇，无论你多大年龄，你都可以继续学习新词汇。

sentences.en: Um, right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对的。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, so that's, that's where we are.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，所以情况就是这样。

sentences.en: So still a lot of work to be done.
sentences.zh: 所以仍有很多工作要做。

sentences.en: Sponsored by Newport Healthcare, dedicated to providing sustainable healing for young people
sentences.zh: 本节目由纽波特医疗保健赞助，致力于为受心理健康问题困扰的

sentences.en: struggling with mental health concerns so they can move from self-destruction to self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 年轻人提供可持续的康复治疗，帮助他们从自我毁灭走向自我接纳。

sentences.en: Based in compassion and driven by outcomes, Newport serves teens and young adults ages 12 to 28 at residential and outpatient programs nationwide.
sentences.zh: 纽波特立足于同理心，以结果为导向，为全国范围内的住宅和门诊项目中的12至28岁青少年及年轻人提供服务。

sentences.en: Through tailored treatment and family support,
sentences.zh: 通过量身定制的治疗和家庭支持，

sentences.en: Newport successfully addresses psychological and behavioral health issues, including depression, anxiety, PTSD, personality disorders, and substance abuse.
sentences.zh: 纽波特成功地解决了心理和行为健康问题，包括抑郁症、焦虑症、创伤后应激障碍、人格障碍和药物滥用。

sentences.en: Learn more at newporthealthcare.com.
sentences.zh: Learn more at newporthealthcare.com.

sentences.en: So going in a slightly different direction, you also study people with brain abnormalities that people might think would hurt their language abilities.
sentences.zh: 接下来转向一个略有不同的方向，你还研究过大脑有异常的人，而人们原本可能会认为这些异常会损害他们的语言能力。

sentences.en: For instance, you recently published a paper about a woman who is missing her left temporal lobe, and yet she's remarkably unaffected by it.
sentences.zh: 例如，你最近发表了一篇论文，关于一位女性失去了左侧颞叶，然而她却完全没有受到明显影响。

sentences.en: She has totally normal language abilities, even exceptional in some ways, because she speaks a second language fluently.
sentences.zh: 她的语言能力完全正常，在某些方面甚至异常出色，因为她能流利地说第二语言。

sentences.en: So what do case studies like that tell us about how language is processed in the brain?
sentences.zh: 那么，这样的个案研究能告诉我们关于语言在人脑中是如何处理的什么信息呢？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is also another line of work that kind of came about somewhat accidentally, because this individual reached out to us and volunteered her brain.
sentences.zh: 这也是另一类有些偶然才出现的研究，因为这个人主动联系了我们并贡献了她的脑部数据。

sentences.en: So she didn't know that anything was different about her brain until she was in her 20s, and she kind of accidentally found out.
sentences.zh: 所以在她20多岁之前，她并不知道自己的大脑有什么不同，她是偶然间发现的。

sentences.en: And it turns out that it's actually not so uncommon, as you might think, to have an unusual brain.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，拥有一个与众不同的大脑其实并不像你想象的那么罕见。

sentences.en: Because our brains have a lot of redundancy and plasticity, especially early on, a lot of early damage goes undetected.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的大脑具有很强的冗余性和可塑性，特别是在生命的早期，许多早期的损伤往往不易被察觉。

sentences.en: So some big event may happen in your brain as you're going through the birth canal or shortly thereafter.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你通过产道或在此之后不久，你的大脑可能会发生某些重大事件。

sentences.en: And you have so much brain tissue to work with that you grow up totally normal.
sentences.zh: 由于你有如此丰富的脑组织可以利用，你长大后依然完全正常。

sentences.en: Sometimes people kind of live their life happily and don't know that they have some big chunk of their brain missing because they don't have any symptoMs. And that means
sentences.zh: 有时人们会开开心心地过完一生，却根本不知道自己大脑很大一部分缺失了，因为他们没有任何症状。这意味着

sentences.en: they don't go to a doctor and they don't get referred to a neurologist or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 他们不会去看医生，也不会被转诊给神经科医生或诸如此类的专家。

sentences.en: There's also evidence from surgical interventions that sometimes are done early on for cases of,
sentences.zh: 来自外科手术干预的证据也表明，有时为了治疗诸如

sentences.en: for example, severe epilepsy, where I don't think they do that quite anymore as severe, but it used to be the case that sometimes whole hemispheres would be removed.
sentences.zh: 严重癫痫等病例，会在早期进行手术。虽然现在他们可能不再做这么严重的手术了，但过去有时确实会切除整个半球。

sentences.en: So hemisperectomy is a surgery that used to be done.
sentences.zh: 因此，大脑半球切除术是过去曾经做过的一种手术。

sentences.en: And again, those kids, if the surgery is done early enough, they grow up and they're relatively fine.
sentences.zh: 同样，如果手术做得足够早，这些孩子长大后也会相对健康。

sentences.en: Sometimes they'll have some motor deficits, but in terms of their cognition, everything seems okay.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会有些运动障碍，但在认知方面，一切似乎都正常。

sentences.en: Now, of course, this is in striking contrast to having a stroke later in life or having a surgical procedure that removes some part of your language cortex later in life,
sentences.zh: 当然，这与成年后遭遇中风或通过外科手术切除部分语言皮层形成鲜明对比，

sentences.en: which will lead to probleMs. And I think you can learn a lot of different things from this population.
sentences.zh: 因为那会导致问题。我认为你可以从这个群体中学到很多不同的东西。

sentences.en: So this paper we published, we asked the question that you couldn't even really ask in any other way.
sentences.zh: 所以我们发表的这篇论文，提出了一个你甚至无法通过其他任何方式提出的问题。

sentences.en: We asked about whether, um, uh, so the language system consists of temporal and frontal areas.
sentences.zh: 我们探讨了，嗯，语言系统由颞叶和额叶区域组成。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Frontal cortical areas like in the front of your head and side of your head, lateral temporal, uh, side of the temporal lobe.
sentences.zh: 额叶皮层区域，比如你头部前方和侧面的区域，还有外侧颞叶，也就是颞叶的侧面。

sentences.en: And typically we see them both, uh, as early as, um, can be measured.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，只要能够被测量到，我们就能很早就同时看到这两者。

sentences.en: Uh, as you said, it's hard to put kids in the scanner.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，把孩子放进扫描仪里很不容易。

sentences.en: So, um, you can do it from about, you know, four or five pretty well, uh, at that age, if you look at their language regions,
sentences.zh: 所以，大约从四五岁开始你就可以做得很好，在这个年龄，如果你观察他们的语言区域，

sentences.en: they have the temporal regions and they have the frontal regions.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有颞叶区域，也拥有额叶区域。

sentences.en: Uh, the question is what is the relationship between them?
sentences.zh: 问题是它们之间的关系是什么？

sentences.en: Do some of them emerge earlier than do the frontal regions emerge later?
sentences.zh: 是其中一些出现得更早，而额叶区域出现得更晚吗？

sentences.en: Because there is also a lot of evidence that frontal lobes in general are slower developing.
sentences.zh: 因为也有大量证据表明，总体而言额叶的发育速度较慢。

sentences.en: And so this individual who grew up without her temporal lobe, left temporal lobe, could allow us to
sentences.zh: 因此，这位在没有左颞叶、左侧颞叶的情况下长大的个人，使我们能够

sentences.en: ask you, would there be responses, neural responses to language in her left frontal cortex, which is perfectly healthy.
sentences.zh: 探究：在她的左侧额叶皮层（这个区域完全健康，其它许多功能都在那里发生）中，是否会对语言产生神经反应？

sentences.en: A lot of other stuff is happening there.
sentences.zh: 许多其他事情都在那里发生。

sentences.en: So would there be some language responses in that, um, uh, part of her brain?
sentences.zh: 那么在她大脑的那个部分，会不会有一些语言反应呢？

sentences.en: And there isn't.
sentences.zh: 结果是没有。

sentences.en: So her language system was totally removed, remapped onto her, um, right hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 所以她的语言系统被完全移除，并重新映射到了她的右半球。

sentences.en: I shouldn't say remapped because there was also claimed that language is originally bilateral, early on bilateral, and then it becomes more lateralized as you grow up.
sentences.zh: 我其实不应该说“重新映射”，因为也有人认为语言最初是双侧的，早期是双侧的，随着成长才变得更加单侧化。

sentences.en: Although that's also controversial, but in any case, her language system is happily living in her
sentences.zh: 尽管这也是有争议的，但无论如何，她的语言系统愉快地安家在了她的

sentences.en: right hemisphere, but, um, unlike in typical individuals where say, if I put you in the scanner,
sentences.zh: 右半球，但是，与正常人不同的是——比方说，如果我把你放进扫描仪里，

sentences.en: you likely will have your language areas on the left, but you'll also have some responses in the right homotopic corresponding areas.
sentences.zh: 你的语言区很可能在左侧，但你在右侧同源的对应区域也会有一些反应。

sentences.en: That's, um, kind of what you typically see.
sentences.zh: 这通常是你所能看到的现象。

sentences.en: And in, um, EG, no matter how much this is this individual without her left temporal lobe, no matter how powerful the tests were that
sentences.zh: 而在脑电图（EEG）中，无论这位没有左颞叶的个人接受了多么强力

sentences.en: we were using to detect language responses, there's just zero response to language anywhere in her
sentences.zh: 的测试来检测语言反应，她在完全健康的左侧额叶中的任何地方，对语言的反应都是绝对零度。

sentences.en: perfectly healthy left frontal lobe, suggesting that perhaps the lack of this temporal cortex, um,
sentences.zh: 这表明，也许正是缺乏这种颞叶皮层，

sentences.en: is, um, what's making these regions not emerge, right?
sentences.zh: 才导致这些区域无法发育，对吧？

sentences.en: So maybe you need these temporal to frontal connections early on to kind of wire up the frontal parts of the language system.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能在早期就需要这些从颞叶到额叶的连接，来构建语言系统的额叶部分。

sentences.en: Uh, but ever since, um, this word got covered by the media, I've had a lot of people write to me
sentences.zh: 但自从这件事被媒体报道以来，有很多人写信给我，

sentences.en: and say, you know, I also have an unusual brain and they will send me like screenshots of their MRIs
sentences.zh: 说“我也有一个不寻常的大脑”，他们会发给我他们MRI的截图，

sentences.en: and they have like their right temporal lobe missing, or their frontal cortex chunks missing, or their parietal lobe missing.
sentences.zh: 展示他们缺失了右颞叶，或者额叶皮层的某些部分，或者顶叶缺失。

sentences.en: And so, um, one question that I think we can very interestingly address in this population is the relationship between language and social cognition.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为我们可以在这个群体中非常有趣地探讨的一个问题，就是语言与社会认知之间的关系。

sentences.en: So language, as we mentioned, is typically in the left hemisphere, present more strongly in the left hemisphere,
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我们所提到的，语言通常位于左半球，在左半球表现得更强烈，

sentences.en: and all sorts of social functions are more strongly present in the right hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 而各种社会功能则更多地存在于右半球。

sentences.en: Now, if you only have one side of your brain, or largely, you know, if a lot of the brain is missing
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你只有大脑的一侧，或者在很大程度上，如果大脑的一侧缺失了许多部分，

sentences.en: on one side, some parts of the, say, social cognition would have to move to the left, or some parts of language would have to move to the right.
sentences.zh: 社会认知的某些部分就不得不转移到左侧，或者语言的某些部分就不得不转移到右侧。

sentences.en: And we want to understand the constraints on how these two systems can coexist within the same hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 我们要了解的是这两个系统如何在同一个半球共存的限制条件。

sentences.en: Like, can they start sharing resources?
sentences.zh: 比如，它们会开始共享资源吗？

sentences.en: Can they actually recruit overlapping bits of the brain and still manifest as typical cognition with no deficits in either language or social processing?
sentences.zh: 它们真的能调用大脑中重叠的区域，同时仍表现出典型的认知能力，且在语言或社交处理上没有丝毫缺陷吗？

sentences.en: Or do they just take up less space and remain fully segregated?
sentences.zh: 还是说它们只是占用更小的空间并完全保持隔离？

sentences.en: Or how, how do they reorganize in such cases?
sentences.zh: 或者说，在那种情况下它们是如何重组的？

sentences.en: So that's where we're going with that work.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们这项研究的方向。

sentences.en: So when you looked at EG, the woman with the missing temporal, left temporal lobe, did she have social deficits?
sentences.zh: 所以，当你观察EG（那个缺少左颞叶的女性）时，她有社交缺陷吗？

sentences.en: Were you looking for that?
sentences.zh: 你当时在寻找这个吗？

sentences.en: She doesn't.
sentences.zh: 她没有。

sentences.en: I mean, we've tested her on some basic stuff.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们对她进行了一些基础测试。

sentences.en: And we even tested her on a pretty extensive battery of so-called pragmatic tasks.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至对她进行了一套相当广泛的所谓语用任务测试。

sentences.en: So these are abilities that are kind of at the junction of language and social cognition.
sentences.zh: 这些能力有点处于语言和社交认知的交汇点上。

sentences.en: So understanding sarcasm or understanding when somebody is asking you a question, but really they want you to do something, right?
sentences.zh: 比如理解讽刺，或者理解当别人问你一个问题时，其实是想让你做某事，对吧？

sentences.en: If I say, can you please pass the salt?
sentences.zh: 如果我说，请把盐递给我好吗？

sentences.en: I'm not really asking you if you can do it.
sentences.zh: 我其实不是在问你能不能做到。

sentences.en: I'm asking you to do it.
sentences.zh: 我是在要求你去做。

sentences.en: That's just the way we do this.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这样交流的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, and she looks absolutely typical on this, you know, or like also things like using contrastive prosody, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，她在这一点上表现得完全很典型，你知道的，或者还有像使用对比语调之类的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Like if I'm emphasizing a sort of part of my message to indicate that, um, something is different from what you might have thought, like, uh, no, I want a red dress, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我强调信息的一部分来表明，嗯，有些事情和你想的不一样，比如，不，我要一件红裙子，对吧？

sentences.en: Suggesting that maybe we were talking about a blue dress before, and I'm contrasting this.
sentences.zh: 这暗示我们之前可能在谈论一件蓝裙子，而我正在做对比。

sentences.en: So these kinds of cues that are at the junction of understanding people's mental states, like tense, like why are they saying it, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，这些线索处于理解人们心理状态的交汇点上，比如意图，为什么他们要这么说，对吧？

sentences.en: Why, why, why are they saying it in this way?
sentences.zh: 为什么，为什么，为什么他们要以这种方式说话？

sentences.en: And linguistic processing, um, seem totally impacted her.
sentences.zh: 而语言处理，嗯，对她来说似乎完全没有受到影响。

sentences.en: I think, I think we can maybe look at more stuff, but really she's like a delightful person.
sentences.zh: 我想，我想我们或许可以研究更多东西，但她真的是一个非常讨人喜欢的人。

sentences.en: And you could, you know, we've now interacted with her for, uh, she's come out, I think three times and, um, you know,
sentences.zh: 你可以，你知道的，我们现在和她互动过，呃，她来过，我想有三次，而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: you would never suspect that anything is different about her brain.
sentences.zh: 你绝不会怀疑她的大脑有什么不同。

sentences.en: Um, so that also tells you that we don't need as much brain as we have.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也说明了我们其实不需要那么多的大脑。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And of course there are surgeons wouldn't, wouldn't, would be out of jobs if, uh, that wasn't the case, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，如果不是这样的话，外科医生就要失业了，对吧？

sentences.en: They'll tell you that there's a lot of stuff you can cut out and even in adults and, um, we're totally fine.
sentences.zh: 他们会告诉你，即使在成年人身上，你也可以切掉很多东西，而且，嗯，我们完全没事。

sentences.en: One question you, you look at that I find really fascinating also is the relationship between language and thought.
sentences.zh: 你研究的另一个让我觉得非常迷人的问题是语言和思考之间的关系。

sentences.en: And for many people, it, it seems intuitive that you couldn't engage in complex thinking if you didn't have language, but you found that's not necessarily the case.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，似乎很直观的一点是：如果没有语言，你就无法进行复杂的思考，但你发现事实并非必然如此。

sentences.en: Can, can you explain how you can have thought without language?
sentences.zh: 你能，你能解释一下怎么在没有语言的情况下进行思考吗？

sentences.en: I think intuitions about our own thinking processes have their limitations.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对自己思考过程的直觉是有局限性的。

sentences.en: Uh, we may have some intuitions about how we think, but really I think empirical data are more compelling.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们可能对我们是如何思考有一些直觉，但实际上我认为实证数据更有说服力。

sentences.en: And so, um, this question of whether you need language to think complex thoughts is a really big and deep one.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，是否需要语言来进行复杂思考这个问题是一个非常重大且深奥的问题。

sentences.en: And there's a very strong propensity historically to link them together because basically the way it goes is, Oh, you know, here's a species of animals, right?
sentences.zh: 历史上有一种非常强烈的倾向将它们联系在一起，因为基本上逻辑是这样的：哦，你看，这有一种动物，对吧？

sentences.en: Humans, they're really smart and they have language.
sentences.zh: 人类，他们真的很聪明，而且他们有语言。

sentences.en: Therefore they're smart because they have language.
sentences.zh: 因此他们聪明是因为他们有语言。

sentences.en: And that logically just doesn't follow at all.
sentences.zh: 从逻辑上讲，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: It could be that there's, they got smart, they got smarter than other animals.
sentences.zh: 很有可能是他们变得聪明了，他们比其他动物更聪明了。

sentences.en: And then the communication system kind of caught up, right?
sentences.zh: 然后交流系统才跟上了节奏，对吧？

sentences.en: Once you have enough mental complexity, um, enough complexity in your thoughts that you want to share them, maybe you then come up with a more
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了足够的心理复杂性，嗯，你的思想中有足够的复杂性，想要与他人分享，也许你就会想出一种更

sentences.en: sophisticated code so that you can share your thoughts with one another.
sentences.zh: 复杂的代码，以便你可以与彼此分享你的想法。

sentences.en: But in terms of evidence, yes, it seems that, um, the language system is relatively silent as, as measured with tools like fMRI.
sentences.zh: 但就证据而言，是的，似乎，嗯，用fMRI等工具测量时，语言系统相对是保持静默的。

sentences.en: When you engage in, you know, playing chess, solving problems, doing math, all sorts of things that you would think would be closely linked to language or relying on linguistic
sentences.zh: 当你从事，你知道的，下棋、解题、做数学，以及各种你认为与语言紧密相连或依赖语言的事情时

sentences.en: representations.
sentences.zh: 表征。

sentences.en: And in individuals with severe aphasia, so severe language problems, you can ask them to do all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 对于患有严重失语症（即严重语言障碍）的个人，你可以让他们做各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: And short of translating them into language, like understanding language or producing language, they can do everything that you and I can do.
sentences.zh: 除了将它们转化为语言（比如理解语言或产生语言）之外，他们能做你和我能做的一切事情。

sentences.en: They can navigate the world.
sentences.zh: 他们可以在世界上穿行。

sentences.en: They can understand others' intentions, as long as you don't have to rely on the verbal cues, right?
sentences.zh: 他们可以理解他人的意图，只要你不必依赖言语线索，对吧？

sentences.en: You can infer it from, um, people's behaviors, actions, um, facial expressions, and things like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以从，嗯，人们的行为、动作、嗯，面部表情之类的事情中推断出来。

sentences.en: They can, um, do Sudoku puzzles.
sentences.zh: 他们可以，嗯，玩数独游戏。

sentences.en: I mean, they can basically, um, they have the same richness of their mental worlds as they did before they had this major stroke event.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们基本上，嗯，他们的精神世界的丰富程度和他们遭遇这次重大中风之前一样。

sentences.en: They just lose the ability to convert those thoughts into a code that other, uh, humans can understand.
sentences.zh: 他们只是失去了将这些想法转化为其他人类能够理解的代码的能力。

sentences.en: But they have language, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们拥有语言，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they, they could speak before the stroke, so they actually have language as opposed to say, like the Helen Keller test, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们中风前会说话，所以他们实际上拥有语言，这与比如说海伦·凯勒测试不同，对吧？

sentences.en: Where she was, you know, a little girl before she actually got language as we understand it.
sentences.zh: 在她真正掌握我们所理解的语言之前，她还是个小女孩。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, so the question is there, like, was it necessary for language to be there early on to get some of these capacities to develop?
sentences.zh: 所以，所以问题就在于，为了让这些能力得以发展，早期必须要有语言的存在吗？

sentences.en: And that's an interesting question because, of course, in these adult stroke cases, you know, everything was, they had both language and they
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的问题，因为当然，在这些成年中风的病例中，你知道，一切都是，他们既有语言又有

sentences.en: had their mentally, you know, um, general intelligence.
sentences.zh: 他们的心理，你知道，嗯，一般智力。

sentences.en: And then at some point, the language system was basically taken out and the rest of cognition seems okay.
sentences.zh: 然后在某个时候，语言系统基本上被拿掉了，而其余的认知看起来似乎没问题。

sentences.en: But maybe if you don't have access to language early on, you can't actually develop the ability to, you know, categorize things in the world or do math or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但也许如果你在早期接触不到语言，你就无法真正发展出对世界上事物进行分类、做数学或类似事情的能力。

sentences.en: And of course, it's much harder to ask that question because you can deprive kids of language, but there are cases where deaf kids are born to hearing
sentences.zh: 当然，要探讨这个问题要困难得多，因为你可以剥夺儿童接触语言的机会，但有些情况下，耳聋儿童出生在听力正常的

sentences.en: parents, which is actually the majority of deaf kids are born to hearing parents.
sentences.zh: 父母家庭，事实上大多数耳聋儿童都出生在听力正常的父母家庭。

sentences.en: And so their parents don't know sign language because they typically wouldn't have had a reason to learn sign language.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的父母不懂手语，因为他们通常没有理由去学手语。

sentences.en: And in some such cases, these kids don't get access to language for sometimes a few years, sometimes parents into their teenage years.
sentences.zh: 在某些这样的情况下，这些孩子有时会有几年，有时甚至到十几岁都接触不到语言。

sentences.en: It hardly ever happens in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国这几乎再也不会发生了

sentences.en: anymore because of all the education
sentences.zh: 由于对耳聋的教育

sentences.en: about deafness and the importance of sign language.
sentences.zh: 以及手语重要性的普及。

sentences.en: But from the anecdotal evidence and some sparse experimental evidence that exists, it seems that, again, most things you can learn without language.
sentences.zh: 但从现有的轶事证据和一些稀疏的实验证据来看，似乎大多数事情你依然可以在没有语言的情况下学习。

sentences.en: Not that it, you know, not that it wouldn't be easier if you had language, but it's not like you can't learn math absent linguistic input.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说，你知道的，倒不是说如果你有语言会不会更轻松，但并不是说在没有语言输入的情况下你就无法学习数学。

sentences.en: And I think there's more work to be done on that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这方面还有更多工作要做。

sentences.en: I think it's a very exciting population that can shed light on this question, but there's only a handful of individuals
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常令人兴奋的群体，可以阐明这个问题，但真正缺乏语言足够长时间以至于产生影响的个体只有区区

sentences.en: who really were lacking language for a long enough time that that would have mattered.
sentences.zh: 几个人。

sentences.en: But I'm trying to team up with a researcher at BU to try to look at this more systematically.
sentences.zh: 但我正试图与波士顿大学的一位研究员合作，试图更系统地研究这一点。

sentences.en: Another area where you're doing research is on artificial intelligence language learning systeMs.
sentences.zh: 你进行研究的另一个领域是人工智能语言学习系统。

sentences.en: Do AI language systems learn language the same way that humans do?
sentences.zh: AI语言系统学习语言的方式和人类一样吗？

sentences.en: Almost certainly not.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定不是。

sentences.en: I mean, they're basically, they have a bunch of text dumped on them, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们基本上是被倾倒了一堆文本，对吧？

sentences.en: That's not at all like we were saying, you know, the way a baby learns is very, very different.
sentences.zh: 这与我们刚才说的完全不同，你知道，婴儿学习的方式非常非常不同。

sentences.en: I mean, and there's many ways in which it's different.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在很多方面它都是不同的。

sentences.en: Like, one, you just get linguistic input and it's completely unrelated from the perceptual and motor experiences in the world, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，第一，你得到的语言输入与世界上感知和运动体验完全无关，对吧？

sentences.en: They just have sequences of words as all they're being fed the models.
sentences.zh: 模型被喂给的全部东西都只是一串串的词语。

sentences.en: And of course, they also don't have any social interactive component, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，它们也没有任何社会互动成分，对吧？

sentences.en: There's no way they can understand intent behind why somebody might say something.
sentences.zh: 它们不可能理解某人说某句话背后的意图。

sentences.en: All they get are co-occurrences among words.
sentences.zh: 它们得到的全都是词语之间的共现。

sentences.en: Now, with a large enough training set, you can get a lot from those co-occurrences.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果有足够大的训练集，你可以从这些共现中获得很多东西。

sentences.en: Language is very powerful in that it reflects all sorts of regularities about the world.
sentences.zh: 语言非常强大，因为它反映了关于世界的各种规律。

sentences.en: And so in some cases, if you have a model generate some coherent text, it's very tempting to think that the model knows something, quote, unquote.
sentences.zh: 所以在某些情况下，如果你让模型生成一些连贯的文本，人们很容易认为该模型“懂”某些东西，加引号的懂。

sentences.en: But of course, it doesn't really, all it knows is linguistic regularities.
sentences.zh: 但当然，它并不是真的懂，它懂的全部只是语言规律。

sentences.en: And it so happens that they reflect some world knowledge, but it's all restricted to the knowledge of language.
sentences.zh: 碰巧这些规律反映了一些世界知识，但它完全局限于语言知识。

sentences.en: The fact that they learn differently doesn't mean that they can't be useful as models of some aspects of language processing behaviorally or in the brain.
sentences.zh: 它们学习方式的不同并不意味着它们不能在行为上或大脑中作为语言处理某些方面的有用模型。

sentences.en: But I think all of these caveats need to be taken into account.
sentences.zh: 但我认为所有这些注意事项都需要考虑进去。

sentences.en: For me, like we just talked about how language is separate from thinking.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，就像我们刚才讨论的语言如何独立于思考。

sentences.en: For us, for my group, I think these models are really great because they're kind of like a clean version of language.
sentences.zh: 对我们而言，对我的团队来说，我认为这些模型真的很棒，因为它们有点像纯净版的语言。

sentences.en: It's like language in a box.
sentences.zh: 就像一个盒子里的语言。

sentences.en: None of the other stuff, perceptual, motor, conceptual is in there, right?
sentences.zh: 没有其他任何东西，感知、运动、概念都不在里面，对吧？

sentences.en: It's just linguistic statistics, which is what I think the human language system is maybe similar to because it's separate from all this other stuff as well.
sentences.zh: 它只是语言统计数据，我认为这或许与人类语言系统有相似之处，因为它也独立于所有这些其他东西之外。

sentences.en: And so we find that in the brain, these models actually capture neural responses to language quite well.
sentences.zh: 因此我们发现在大脑中，这些模型实际上相当好地捕捉到了对语言的神经反应。

sentences.en: But of course, if we want to build models, they can capture responses to language understanding in a deep sense, right?
sentences.zh: 但当然，如果我们想要构建模型，它们可以在深层意义上捕捉到对语言理解的反应，对吧？

sentences.en: Like reasoning on representations that we get from language.
sentences.zh: 比如对我们从语言中获得的表征进行推理。

sentences.en: So it's not just kind of getting some coarse approximation of meaning, but actually doing some downstream reasoning on the things we get from linguistic input.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅仅是获得对意义的某种粗略近似，而是对我们从语言输入中获得的事物进行下游推理。

sentences.en: Then I think we'll want to supplement these statistical language models with models of actual aspects of thought and reasoning, including
sentences.zh: 那么我想我们将需要用实际的思考和推理方面的模型来补充这些统计语言模型，包括

sentences.en: social, social modeling of social, like mental states.
sentences.zh: 社会的、对社会的建模，比如心理状态。

sentences.en: And there's exciting work happening in that direction at MIT and other places.
sentences.zh: 麻省理工学院和其他地方正在朝着这个方向开展令人兴奋的研究。

sentences.en: So what else are you working on next?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来你还在研究什么？

sentences.en: I mean, what are the big questions that you still want to answer?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你仍然想解答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: Trying to use artificial neural network models as models of the mind and brain, I think it's a very promising direction.
sentences.zh: 试图将人工神经网络模型用作心智和大卫的模型，我认为这是一个非常有前景的方向。

sentences.en: I think it's for the first time in the history of the kind of language research,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是在某种语言研究历史上的第一次，

sentences.en: where we potentially can have some kind of a close to an algorithmic level understanding of how language processing might happen.
sentences.zh: 我们有可能对语言处理可能是如何发生的有一种接近算法层面的理解。

sentences.en: And we can go beyond putting words like syntax on some blob on your brain and just leaving it at that, which is where the state of the art has been for many years.
sentences.zh: 我们可以超越那种把诸如句法之类的词安在大脑的某个区域然后就不管了的做法，而多年来这正是该领域的最新技术水平。

sentences.en: But now we can actually build some, you know, fully implemented models that do something that at least in some aspects looks similar to humans.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们实际上可以构建一些，你知道的，完全实现的模型，它们所做的事情至少在某些方面看起来与人类相似。

sentences.en: Of course, the goal here for us as scientists is not to build a model that's as close to the brain as possible, although that is one goal, because then it can also afford
sentences.zh: 当然，我们作为科学家的目标不是构建一个尽可能接近大脑的模型，尽管这也是一个目标，因为那样它也能提供

sentences.en: certain things.
sentences.zh: 某些东西。

sentences.en: But I'm more excited to understand what it is about these models that leads them to capture something about human behavior or human neural response.
sentences.zh: 但我更渴望理解这些模型的什么特性使它们能够捕捉到人类行为或人类神经反应的某些特征。

sentences.en: And so we're doing a lot of experimentation now on these models, messing with them in various ways, because we have full access to them, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在对这些模型做了大量的实验，用各种方式对它们进行干预，因为我们对它们拥有完全的访问权限，对吧？

sentences.en: We can lesion them, we can train them in different ways, we can mess with their architectures,
sentences.zh: 我们可以对它们进行损毁，用不同的方式训练它们，干扰它们的架构，

sentences.en: and try to see what are the properties that the model needs to have to provide a good fit to human cognitive or neural mental spaces.
sentences.zh: 并试图看看模型需要具备哪些属性才能很好地契合人类认知或神经心智空间。

sentences.en: And I'm also very excited to try to understand how language develops.
sentences.zh: 我也非常渴望去理解语言是如何发展的。

sentences.en: So I'm involved in some collaborations.
sentences.zh: 所以我参与了一些合作。

sentences.en: It's a very hard, painstaking effort to try to collect neural responses from young kids, because most of the action is happening between say,
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常艰巨、细致的工作，试图收集幼儿的神经反应，因为大部分活动都发生在，比方说，

sentences.en: I don't know, like nine months and kind of two years.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，大概在九个月到两岁左右。

sentences.en: Like that's the sweet spot of development where language kind of comes to be.
sentences.zh: 就像那是语言开始萌芽的发展黄金期。

sentences.en: It still develops a little bit after that, but really the bulk of it is there by like two and a half, three, like it's, you know, almost all there.
sentences.zh: 在此之后它还会继续发展一点，但实际上它的绝大部分在两岁半、三岁时就已经具备了，就像是，你知道的，几乎全部都在那里了。

sentences.en: And there are people here and then a few other groups trying to develop tools to be able to test
sentences.zh: 这里的人们和其他一些研究小组正在努力开发工具，以便能够测试

sentences.en: younger kids in the scanner with silent sequences, really fun paradigms, all sorts of kind of ingenuity, experimental ingenuity.
sentences.zh: 年龄更小的孩子，让他们在扫描仪里听静音序列，使用真正有趣的范式，以及各种各样的独创性、实验独创性。

sentences.en: And I think that could be another window to try to understand how language may relate to general reasoning abilities, as well as to kind of social perception,
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能成为试图理解语言如何与一般推理能力以及社会知觉相关联的另一扇窗户，

sentences.en: cognition, by looking at whether perhaps language shows, early language areas show more overlap with,
sentences.zh: 认知，通过观察早期的语言区域是否表现出更多的重叠，

sentences.en: for example, brain regions that support general kind of thinking and reasoning, or areas that support some aspects of processing con-specifics, right?
sentences.zh: 例如，与支持一般思考和推理的大脑区域，或者支持处理同类（同种个体）某些方面的区域重叠，对吧？

sentences.en: Processing facial expressions, body language,
sentences.zh: 处理面部表情、身体语言，

sentences.en: thinking about others' intents, and things like that.
sentences.zh: 思考他人的意图等等。

sentences.en: So hopefully in the next few decades we can make some headway.
sentences.zh: 所以希望在未来几十年里我们能取得一些进展。

sentences.en: Or maybe sooner.
sentences.zh: 或者可能更早。

sentences.en: Well, those are big questions, and this is really great, great work that you're doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些都是宏大的问题，你所做的工作真的非常非常棒。

sentences.en: Very interesting.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for joining me today, Dr. Fedorenko.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天能来，费多连科博士。

sentences.en: That was really fun, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 上，或者在 Apple、Stitcher 以及你今天收听播客的任何地方找到往期的《心理学对话》节目。

sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢你听到的内容，请给我们写条评论。

sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发电子邮件到 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。
